patient_information: A 32-year-old Malawian man, HIV positive, started on antiretroviral therapy (ART) and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis 2 months earlier, with a recent CD4 count of 95 cells/µL, and a history of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) sputum smear-negative pulmonary tuberculosis 12 years ago.
chief_complaint: A 6-week history of productive cough and chest pain, associated with weight loss, fevers, night sweats, and a painful, swollen neck.
history_of_present_illness: A 32-year-old Malawian man presented with a 6-week history of productive cough, chest pain, weight loss, fevers, night sweats, and a painful, swollen neck, with no other symptoms; he was HIV positive and started on ART and co-trimoxazole 2 months prior, and had been treated for AFB sputum smear-negative pulmonary tuberculosis 12 years ago.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is a Malawian man, HIV positive, with a history of pulmonary tuberculosis, and denied leaving Malawi where multi-drug resistance for TB is uncommon.
vitals: Temperature 39.2°C (102.56°F), pulse 112 bpm, respiratory rate 28 breath cycles per minute, and normal blood pressure.
physical_exam: The patient appeared moderately ill, pale, and sweating, with large, matted, and later increasingly fluctuant, lymph glands palpable in his neck; the rest of the examination was unremarkable.
labs_and_diagnostics: Initial full blood count showed WBC 14.3×10^9/L, haemoglobin 6.3 g/dL, MCV 66 fL, platelets 246 × 10^9/L; three sputum samples were negative for AFB; fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of a neck gland yielded purulent material with AFB 2+ positive microscopy and no growth on blood culture. Later, CD4 count was 109 cells/µL, HIV-1 RNA <400 copies/mL; repeat FBC showed WBC 7.8 × 10^9/L, haemoglobin 6.7 g/dL, MCV 84 fL, platelets 428 × 10^9/L; second FNA showed frank yellowish pus with numerous coccoid bacteria and polymorphonuclear lymphocytes, but bacterial culture results were never received.
differential_diagnosis: Tuberculous lymphadenitis with immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) of the unmasking type, atypical mycobacteria, non-adherence, malabsorption, drug resistance, bacterial lymphadenitis, lymphoma, and later, superimposed bacterial lymphadenitis likely caused by Staphylococcus aureus or paradoxical IRIS.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was admitted and started on TB repeat treatment with streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, while continuing ART; despite this, he did not improve after 3 weeks, with persistent fevers, night sweats, lack of appetite, and worsening, fluctuant neck glands, leading to the initiation of corticosteroids; he subsequently recovered well after incision and drainage, antibiotic treatment, and a short course of corticosteroids, while continuing TB treatment and ART.
final_diagnosis: Tuberculous lymphadenitis with immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) of the unmasking type, complicated by superimposed bacterial lymphadenitis, most likely Staphylococcus aureus.
